messages.subject: Re: Error messages after updating to ggplot2 v 0.9.3
parts:
Hi:

Those are not error messages, but simply messages. It's possible that
some code checks in the development version were not completely
cleaned up prior to release.

Here's what I got in the Rgui console when working on a plot in
another post this morning...for one plot.

> p <- ggplot(results)
The following `from` values were not present in `x`: col, color, pch,
cex, lty, lwd, srt, adj, bg, fg, min, max
> p <- p + aes(x = seq(x = xmin, xmax, length.out = 100))
The following `from` values were not present in `x`: col, color, pch,
cex, lty, lwd, srt, adj, bg, fg, min, max
> p <- p + geom_linerange(aes(ymin = hpdLower, ymax = hpdUpper, x = patient, color = statistic), size = 1.2, width = .75, position = position_dodge(width = dodge))
The following `from` values were not present in `x`: col, pch, cex,

messages.subject: Re: Error messages after updating to ggplot2 v 0.9.3
parts:
Follow-up:

After reading Winston's post in another thread, I started a new
session and reinstalled ggplot2 and plyr (along with evaluate, gtable
and scales just to be sure :). I then tried
Maga's example again:

> library(ggplot2)
> library(plyr)

> df <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 10)),
+ y = rnorm(30))
> # Compute sample mean and standard deviation in each group
> library(plyr)
> ds <- ddply(df, .(gp), summarise, mean = mean(y), sd = sd(y))
>
> # Declare the data frame and common aesthetics.
> # The summary data frame ds is used to plot
> # larger red points in a second geom_point() layer.
> # If the data = argument is not specified, it uses the
> # declared data frame from ggplot(); ditto for the aesthetics.
> ggplot(df, aes(x = gp, y = y)) +
+ geom_point() +
+ geom_point(data = ds, aes(y = mean),
+ colour = 'red', size = 3)
>

The plot now renders fine and there are no messages in the console, as
the above copy/paste from the console shows. (Note the screen prompt
at the end of the snippet.) Thanks to Winston for the explanation at
the RStudio blog - I imagine it's been a hectic day or two for him
replying to all of these inquiries...

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Error messages after updating to ggplot2 v 0.9.3
parts:
I just installed from a clean session in Windows XP, and I'm running into the problem now! But this only seems to happen on Windows.

Unfortunately, I have to run and do something else right now but I'll try to investigate later.

In the meantime, it's probably best to do install.packages(c("ggplot2", "gtable", "scales", "plyr")), and not use dep=T.

-Winston

On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 1:19 PM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
Follow-up:

After reading Winston's post in another thread, I started a new
session and reinstalled ggplot2 and plyr (along with evaluate, gtable
and scales just to be sure :). I then tried
Maga's example again:

> library(ggplot2)
> library(plyr)
> df <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 10)),
+                  y = rnorm(30))
> # Compute sample mean and standard deviation in each group
> library(plyr)
> ds <- ddply(df, .(gp), summarise, mean = mean(y), sd = sd(y))
>
> # Declare the data frame and common aesthetics.
> # The summary data frame ds is used to plot
> # larger red points in a second geom_point() layer.
> # If the data = argument is not specified, it uses the
> # declared data frame from ggplot(); ditto for the aesthetics.
> ggplot(df, aes(x = gp, y = y)) +
+     geom_point() +
+     geom_point(data = ds, aes(y = mean),
+                colour = 'red', size = 3)
>

The plot now renders fine and there are no messages in the console, as
the above copy/paste from the console shows. (Note the screen prompt
at the end of the snippet.) Thanks to Winston for the explanation at
the RStudio blog - I imagine it's been a hectic day or two for him
replying to all of these inquiries...

Dennis
